thematic_title: Map It, Move It — Grade 3 Geometry
descriptive_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Demonstrations — Geometry in 2D and 3D (E1.1-E1.4)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.E1.1: sort, construct, and identify cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, and cones by comparing their faces, edges, vertices, and angles
curriculum_expectations.E1.2: compose and decompose various structures, and identify the two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects that these structures contain
curriculum_expectations.E1.3: identify congruent lengths, angles, and faces of three-dimensional objects by mentally and physically matching them, and determine if the objects are congruent
curriculum_expectations.E1.4: give and follow multistep instructions involving movement from one location to another, including distances and half- and quarter-turns

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 3 unit on geometry (E1.1-E1.4) framed around 'Map It, Move It' — Trekker Tig the Tiger Cub and Compass Coco the Cat. Day 1 sorts 5 named 3D solids by faces, edges, and vertices. Day 2 composes and decomposes structures from 3D objects. Day 3 identifies congruent faces, lengths, and angles. Day 4 gives and follows multistep movement directions with quarter and half turns. Day 5 closes with a Big Map Capstone integrating all 4 expectations. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will sort 3D solids by attributes, compose and decompose structures, identify congruent parts, and give and follow movement directions with turns.

lesson_arc.big_idea: 5 named solids: cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones. Sort by FACES, EDGES, VERTICES.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can sort 5 named solids by faces, edges, and vertices.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Trekker Tig sorts 15 solids; children identify all 5 types.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Bigger structures are MADE OF smaller 2D shapes and 3D objects.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compose and decompose a structure into its parts.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tig builds a tower from cubes and prisms; children decompose 4 structures.

lesson_arc.big_idea: CONGRUENT means SAME SIZE and SAME SHAPE. We match faces, lengths, and angles.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can identify congruent faces, lengths, and angles.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Compass Coco matches 6 face pairs; children check for congruence.

lesson_arc.big_idea: MULTISTEP MOVEMENT uses STEPS plus QUARTER (90°) or HALF (180°) turns.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can give and follow movement directions with turns.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Coco navigates a 5-step map; children give and follow 4-step routes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Geometers SORT solids, BUILD structures, MATCH congruent parts, and FOLLOW maps.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can sort, build, match, and follow movement directions.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children rotate through 4 stations: sort, build, match, follow.

recurring_characters.name: Trekker Tig the Tiger Cub
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Geometry guide. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young tiger cub with a backpack and a 3D-shape sorting basket, holding a measuring tape.

recurring_characters.name: Compass Coco the Cat
recurring_characters.role: Tig's partner. Map+turn character. Cameo Lessons 3-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A small cat with a compass around its neck and a treasure-map clipboard.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: A FLAT side of a 3D shape.
A LINE where two faces meet.
A 3D shape with 2 same ends and rectangle sides.
A 3D shape with a flat base and triangle sides meeting at the top.
Put together — build a structure from parts.
Take apart — break a structure into parts.
Turn 90 degrees — a quarter of a full circle.
Turn 180 degrees — a half of a full circle.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 3 names 5 solids by attribute (cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones).
E1.3 introduces CONGRUENT — same size AND same shape.
E1.4 adds quarter and half turns to multistep movement.
Hands-on with paper solids preferred; physical manipulation builds spatial sense.
